title: Hold a mango cheek steady, score it into a grid down to but not through the skin, then push the skin up to fan the cubes
instruction: Steady the mango cheek, score its flesh into a crosshatch grid of at least 10 cubes down to the skin with the paring knife without cutting through the skin, press the skin side onto the upturned ramekin so the cubes fan out, then leave the cheek, the knife and the ramekin on the board and let go.
context: The usual way to cube a mango: cut a cheek off beside the seed, then (mango.org) "Score (slice) the flesh in a crosshatch pattern, without cutting through the skin" and push the skin's centre up so the cubes fan out. The skin under the flat cut face is a cup, 24 mm deep in the middle and nothing at the edge, so the knife point must follow it down and up on every cut: too shallow and the cubes stay joined, too deep and the skin is cut.
setup: Station bench, top z=0.7475 m; x away from the robot, y to its left. OXO Good Grips 11272900 polypropylene cutting board, 535.9 x 368.3 mm, 16 mm thick (estimated), fixed, centre (0.29, 0), long side along y, top z=0.7635. One cheek of a ripe Ataulfo (Honey) mango, cut off beside the seed by the assessor at reset, lying skin side down: flat cut face 112 x 72 mm, 25.5 mm deep at the middle (24 mm flesh on 1.5 mm skin), outer skin half an ellipsoid, 115 g (estimates; acceptance bands in README). Mercer Millennia M23900P paring knife (76 mm blade, 100 x 22 x 24 mm handle, 50 g; handle and mass estimated) standing on the flat underside of its handle (a pea-sized dab of reusable putty under it in a real trial), blade pointing -y. Upturned white porcelain 2 fl oz ramekin (modelled 60 mm rim, 48 mm flat base, 32 mm tall, 100 g, estimated; in a real trial any porcelain ramekin with a flat base 46-50 mm across and 30-35 mm tall), loose. Steel ruler 300 x 20 x 2 mm beyond the board at (0.49, 0). Lot A (screenshot): cheek cut-face centre (0.310, -0.090), long axis 45 degrees right of straight ahead, narrow end toward the left arm; knife handle centre (0.240, -0.135); ramekin (0.410, -0.210). Lot B: cheek (0.300, -0.072), long axis 33 degrees right of ahead; knife (0.215, -0.140); ramekin (0.400, -0.200). No jitter; the simulation checks each start within 4 mm and 3 degrees.
scoring: Score 0 for the trial if at any moment: any part of the blade (edge, either face or spine) goes more than 1 mm into the 1.5 mm skin more than 2 mm in from the cheek's edge (cut through); the blade touches a gripper or comes within 10 mm of a gripper not holding the knife by its handle; while a gripper holds the cheek, the ramekin, base up relative to the cheek, pressing on the skin from below goes more than 35 mm into it, 9.5 mm past flat (an over-push, the stand-in for split skin; a ramekin on the cut-face side of the cheek, brought down onto it from that side, slid in through its side more than about 5 mm above the skin's lowest point, or under a cheek turned face down never counts as a push or split and meets no resistance). Otherwise judged at the end, with both grippers at least 5 mm from cheek, knife and ramekin, the cheek skin side down on the board, knife and ramekin resting on the board, no blade within 2 mm of the cheek, and nothing moving over 1 mm or 2 degrees for 1 s; if not, 0. A cube is a piece of the cut face separated from every other by cuts reaching within 6 mm of the skin (flesh within 7 mm of the edge is rim), 80-800 mm2 on top, no two points over 30 mm apart. 1.0: at least 10 cubes, and after they were cut the skin's middle was pushed up at least 28 mm onto the ramekin's base (base centre within 15 mm of the middle, the press begun with the base touching the skin from below the cut face) against the full 5 N skin-bending resistance, while a gripper pinched the cheek within 30 degrees of level: the 25.5 mm cup turned 2.5 mm past flat, its middle above the rim, so the cuts open and the cubes fan apart. 0.75: at least 10 cubes, not pushed 28 mm. 0.5: 5-9 cubes. 0.25: one connected run of cut flesh (within 6 mm of the skin, outside the 7 mm rim) whose bounding box is 30 mm or more corner to corner. 0: otherwise. A cut counts only with the knife held by its handle, the cheek pinched by the other hand (opening 10-90 mm, both fingertips within 3 mm of the cheek, contacts 15 mm or more apart), the blade within 45 degrees of upright, the edge moving at 1 mm/s or more within 45 degrees of its own plane, against the stated drag; cuts after the full push do not count. Real trial: a cut counts where it parts the flesh to within 6 mm of the skin, made while the other gripper held the cheek (top video); top photo with the ruler to count and measure cubes; knife tip and depth gauge for cut depth; the skin held to a light for slits or tears, which score 0 (the simulation's 1 mm skin rule is a stricter stand-in for a slit, and its 35 mm over-push limit a stand-in for a split); side video with a 1 mm scale for the push: the held, level cheek's rim comes down to 2.5 mm or more below the ramekin's base, base centre within 15 mm of the skin's middle (top video); side and top videos for the 10 mm blade gap and the end conditions. Lots A and B averaged.
run_limit: 2,400 steps (120 s at 20 Hz) per trial
reset_notes: Real trial: a new Ataulfo (Honey) mango (280-350 g; a 10 N press with a 20 mm flat probe dents it 2-4 mm; no bruises) per trial. The assessor stands it on its stem end and cuts one cheek off about 6 mm beside the centre line, clearing the seed; keep it if the cut face is 105-120 mm long and 66-78 mm wide and 23-28 mm deep at the middle, else cut the other side or a new fruit. Weigh and photograph it with the ruler. Fruit is ripened and kept at 18-24 C, not refrigerated, and used the day it passes the press check. Once per session, a spare scored cheek pressed on the ramekin standing on a kitchen scale records the push resistance (declared 2 N at 10 mm, 5 N at the full push; under half or over twice is reported as a mismatch). Board, knife and ramekin washed and dried. Keeping juice off the shared rig: on both grippers, nitrile finger cots taped over the cut-resistant pad covers (counted in the grasp width), plastic sleeves over gripper bodies and wrists, cameras behind film, a clear 0.1 mm sheet taped under and around the board (height unchanged); after each trial bin the cots, wash or replace the covers, wipe fingers, sleeves and wrists (damp cloth, then 70% isopropyl) and check with a white paper towel. Each session, and any change of covers, cots or tape, starts with a practice trial, then a towel check of the bare fingers, grippers and wrists: trials start only if every towel stays clean. About 12 minutes per trial: 2 to cut and check the cheek, 5 for the checks after the run, 5 to clean and refit covers. Simulation: each trial writes the lot's exact start poses and resets the cut record.
fidelity: True size. Rigid 115 g cheek; blade has no collider. Declared cut: a 1 mm cell is cut where the held, upright edge passes within 6 mm of the 1.5 mm skin, cheek pinched, against up to 1 N drag and 1 N feed (estimates). The ramekin passes into the rigid cheek against a declared skin-bending force (0.2 N/mm to 5 N, rising at most 0.5 N per step, equal reaction; estimate); 28 mm of overlap counts as the skin turned out. The cheek does not deform or show cubes fanning; cuts show as dark 4 mm marks.
scores: demo: 1.0 (lot A 1.0, lot B 1.0); Dream-1 run: 0.0 (lot A 0.0, lot B 0.0, step limit in both); both on the revised task
